title: Freya and the Signal
premise: Rosalind Sterling navigates the colony ship Meridian, whose hold holds two thousand cryosleep backups—half from the founding families, half from the laborers who built the ship—while the colony below them dies of a signal-silence no one will investigate. When a deep-space vessel returns with its crew biologically aged backward and carrying proof that the colony's death was ordered, not accidental, Rosalind must choose between the law that protects the founders' backups and the justice owed to the forgotten. In the end he wakes the laborers' half before the jump window closes, stays behind with the dying colony's last survivor—the woman he loves—and lets the ship go without him.
about_author: A. M. Sterling is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to frequencies no one answered before turning to fiction. They write near-future science fiction about people who keep records when institutions won't.

chapters.title: The Hold Below
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. During a routine navigation shift, Rosalind descends into the cryo-hold and logs the two thousand sleeping backups, noting how the manifest quietly ranks them by family name. He records an unauthorized audio diary about the colony going silent below. Emotional beat: quiet dread and complicity—he knows the system is unjust and has done nothing.

chapters.title: Silence Is a Decision
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Command declares the colony's silence a technical fault and schedules departure for the jump window in ninety days. Rosalind confronts Ilsa Vane, the communications officer he loves, who admits she was ordered to stop transmitting inquiries. Emotional beat: love strained by duty; Rosalind begins keeping evidence instead of just feelings.

chapters.title: What Came Back
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. A derelict vessel answers a hail: the survey crew sent out eleven years ago, returned young—younger than when they left—with no memory of the gap. Their bodies were rebuilt from backups they never consented to. Emotional beat: uncanny wonder curdling into horror as Ilsa realizes someone has been editing people.

chapters.title: The Younger Crew
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind is assigned to debrief the returned crew because he can read their navigation logs. Their star charts show the colony's silence was caused by a deliberate jamming order—one signed by Meridian's own command lineage. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by the realization that his superiors are the culprits.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Command moves up the jump window to sixty days and orders the returned crew quarantined as 'unstable.' Ilsa smuggles Rosalind into quarantine; one of the young crew recognizes her voice from a transmission she made years ago and was punished for. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in secrecy; the two commit to each other and to the truth.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Cross-referencing the backup manifests with the jamming order, Rosalind proves the laborers' backups were scheduled to be jettisoned at the jump point—discarded as dead weight. The founders' half will wake on the new world. Emotional beat: cold fury; justice stops being abstract and becomes a countdown.

chapters.title: The Vote That Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Rosalind and Ilsa take the evidence to the crew council, but command invokes emergency law, seals the hold, and brands them mutineers. Ilsa chooses duty against herself—she reports her own part in the silenced transmissions to buy credibility. Emotional beat: sacrifice; the law turns against them precisely when they need it most.

chapters.title: Breaking the Hold
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. With the jump window hours away, Rosalind uses his navigator's authority to override the hold's environmental locks, waking the laborers' backups first while Vane's loyalists storm the deck. The returned young crew side with him—they know what it is to be woken without consent, and choose to give others the choice they never had. Emotional beat: climax; irreversible action taken outside the law.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Command capitulates rather than kill two thousand witnesses, but the jump window closes in minutes and there is room for only one navigator. Rosalind gives Ilsa the chair—she carries the evidence, the living, and the future. He stays behind with the colony's last survivor, an old woman still transmitting from the surface. Emotional beat: love against duty, resolved by choosing both at terrible cost.

chapters.title: The Signal Continues
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind, epistolary. On the surface, Rosalind helps rebuild the colony around the old transmitter, sending logs toward wherever the Meridian jumped. Years later, a reply arrives—not from the ship, but from the young crew, who left copies of his recordings everywhere they went. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; memory preserved, justice incomplete but alive, love carried forward in signal form.
